t: Masinissa united the Massylii and Masaesyli after Zama in 202 BCE, creating a Berber kingdom centred on Cirta.
Its light cavalry was famed across the Mediterranean, and Punic was the language of its court and towns.
Jugurtha's war with Rome (112–105 BCE) exposed Roman corruption, and Caesar annexed the kingdom after Thapsus in 46 BCE.
dyk: The historian Sallust, whose Jugurthine War is the main account of Numidia, was the first governor of the Roman province that replaced the kingdom.
ev: Masinissa leaves Carthage and allies with Scipio
Masinissa's cavalry helps Rome win the Battle of Zama; Numidia is united
Masinissa defeats Carthage, giving Rome a pretext for the Third Punic War
Masinissa dies; royal powers are divided among his sons
Jugurtha takes Cirta and kills Adherbal and Italian traders
Bocchus I hands Jugurtha over to Sulla
Caesar defeats Juba I at Thapsus and creates the province of Africa Nova
